summary.description: Tetrachloroethylene is a colourless, highly volatile liquid with a distinctive sweet smell. It is primarily used as a dry-cleaning agent for textiles and fabrics, as well as for metal degreasing and in some consumer products.
emission_sources: Use in dry-cleaning of textiles and fabrics
Use as a metal degreasing agent
environmental_impact: Exposure to high levels may affect brain, eyes, kidneys, liver, skin, throat and may cause cancer
PER evaporates readily into the air from water and soil
In the air, it is broken down by sunlight or washed back to soil/water by rain
Slow biodegradation by microorganisms in soil and water

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: Tetrachloroethylene exposure at high levels can cause serious health effects including damage to vital organs and cancer risk, impacting human health significantly.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: The pollutant’s release primarily comes from industrial and consumer use, requiring improved management and sustainable practices to reduce emissions.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: PER can contaminate soil and water, with potential to pollute water resources before evaporating, affecting water quality and safety.
